original_question: If X is a quartic threefold, are the stability conditions sigma(s, q, mu) on its Kuznetsov component Serre-invariant for some choice of (s, q)?
target_in_paper: Question 6.35 in Section 6.5: the paper asks, after separating the degree-4 index-1 case into quartic threefolds versus double covers of quadrics, “If X is a quartic threefold, are the stability conditions σ(s,q,μ) Serre-invariant for some (s,q)?” ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target: it names the correct variety class (quartic threefold), the correct category (its Kuznetsov component), the correct family of induced stability conditions σ(s,q,μ), and the correct property to test (Serre-invariance). It also stays on the exact open problem posed in the paper, rather than drifting to the neighboring Torelli question. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))
missing_details: You should specify that a quartic threefold means a smooth hypersurface of degree 4 in P^4. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))

To make the ambient category stand-alone, you should state that for this genus-3 index-1 Fano case one has Db(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X⟩. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))

You should define what “Serre-invariant” means: there exists an element g̃ in the universal cover of GL_2^+(R) such that S_{Ku(X)}·σ = σ·g̃. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))

You should identify σ(s,q,μ) as the induced Bridgeland stability condition from the Section 6.3 construction, with heart A(s,q,μ)=Coh_{s,q}^μ(X) ∩ Ku(X) and central charge Z(s,q,μ)=Z_{s,q}^μ restricted to Ku(X). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))

You should make the admissible parameter range explicit: (s,q) must lie in Δ={(s,q) in R^2 : q > (1/2)s^2} and satisfy q < -s/2, while μ must satisfy μ_{s,q}(O_X(-H_X)[1]) ≤ μ < μ_{s,q}(O_X). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))

If you want the field assumption fully explicit, the stability-condition discussion is carried out over C there, with the remark that the same proof should work over any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))
refined_question: Let X ⊂ P^4 be a smooth quartic threefold over C, so that Db(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X⟩. Consider the Bridgeland stability conditions σ(s,q,μ)=(A(s,q,μ), Z(s,q,μ)) on Ku(X) obtained by the Section 6.3 induction procedure from the weak stability conditions σ_{s,q}, where (s,q) lies in Δ={(s,q) in R^2 : q > (1/2)s^2} and satisfies q < -s/2, and μ is any real number with μ_{s,q}(O_X(-H_X)[1]) ≤ μ < μ_{s,q}(O_X). Does there exist such an admissible choice of parameters for which σ(s,q,μ) is Serre-invariant, i.e. satisfies S_{Ku(X)}·σ = σ·g̃ for some g̃ in the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)? ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))
justification: The draft is essentially an abbreviated restatement of Question 6.35. The surrounding paragraph in Section 6.5 first explains that for degree 4 there are two families and that, for the non-quartic family (double covers of quadrics), the induced σ(s,q,μ) are not Serre-invariant; the authors then explicitly say they focus on quartic threefolds and pose Question 6.35. To make the question stand-alone, one must import the geometric meaning of “quartic threefold” from Remark 3.14, the description of the Kuznetsov component for genus 3 from (3.3), the definition of Serre-invariance from Definition 6.11, and the notation/parameter constraints for σ(s,q,μ) from Theorem 6.17 and equation (6.7). ([link.springer.com](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12215-022-00796-x))
